source: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet and NASA Solar System Exploration. Moon counts change as new moons are found.

habitableZoneAU.source: Kopparapu et al. 2013 (conservative habitable zone for the Sun)

mercury.fact: The smallest planet. A single day lasts longer than its year!

venus.tempC: About 464 °C, hot enough to melt lead
venus.fact: The hottest planet, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun. Its thick air traps heat.

earth.fact: The only world known to have life, and liquid water on its surface.

mars.atmosphere: 95% carbon dioxide, very thin (under 1% of Earth's)
mars.fact: Home of Olympus Mons, the tallest volcano in the Solar System, about 22 km high.

jupiter.fact: Its Great Red Spot is a storm bigger than Earth that has raged for centuries.

saturn.fact: It is less dense than water. Its rings are hundreds of thousands of km wide but mostly tens of metres thick.

uranus.atmosphere: Hydrogen, helium and methane (which makes it blue-green)
uranus.fact: It is tipped over by 98°, so each pole gets 42 years of sunlight, then 42 years of darkness.

neptune.fact: It has the fastest winds in the Solar System, over 2,000 km/h. It was found by maths before anyone saw it (1846).

earth.name: The Moon
earth.fact: Always shows us the same face. Humans walked on it in 1969–1972, and India's Vikram landed near its south pole in 2023.

mars.name: Phobos
mars.fact: Orbits faster than Mars spins, so it rises in the west. It is slowly spiralling inwards.

mars.name: Deimos
mars.fact: One of the smallest moons known: from Mars it looks like a bright star.

jupiter.name: Io
jupiter.fact: The most volcanic world known, with hundreds of active volcanoes.

jupiter.name: Europa
jupiter.fact: An ocean of liquid water lies under its icy shell: a top place to look for life.

jupiter.name: Ganymede
jupiter.fact: The largest moon in the Solar System, bigger than Mercury, with its own magnetic field.

jupiter.name: Callisto
jupiter.fact: One of the most heavily cratered surfaces in the Solar System.

saturn.name: Titan
saturn.fact: Has a thick orange atmosphere and lakes of liquid methane. Huygens landed there in 2005.

saturn.name: Enceladus
saturn.fact: Shoots fountains of water ice from an ocean under its south pole.

saturn.name: Mimas
saturn.fact: A giant crater, Herschel, covers almost a third of its width.

saturn.name: Rhea
saturn.fact: Saturn's second-largest moon, an icy and cratered world.

saturn.name: Iapetus
saturn.fact: Two-toned: one side is as dark as coal, the other bright as snow.

uranus.name: Titania
uranus.fact: Uranus's largest moon, with huge canyons.

uranus.name: Oberon
uranus.fact: The outermost of Uranus's big moons, old and heavily cratered.

uranus.name: Miranda
uranus.fact: Has Verona Rupes, a cliff thought to be about 20 km tall, among the tallest known.

neptune.name: Triton
neptune.fact: Orbits the wrong way round and has nitrogen geysers. It was probably captured from the Kuiper Belt.
